articleguidance-default-outline-instruct:
Wikipedia covers subjects that have received significant coverage in reliable sources that are independent of the subject. Before you write, check that such coverage exists. If it does not, the article is likely to be deleted however well it is written.

Quick considerations:
* Summarise what independent sources say. Do not add your own analysis, opinion or conclusions.
* Open with a short lead that says what the subject is and why it is notable.
* Cite a source for every claim that a reader could reasonably question.
* Write in a neutral tone. Avoid promotional language and loaded words.
* Do not write about yourself, your employer, your family or your friends.
* Do not copy text from other websites or books. Write it in your own words.
articleguidance-default-outline-recommen: News organisations with editorial oversight and a record of fact-checking
Peer-reviewed academic journals and books from academic publishers
Books from established publishers and reference works with named editors
articleguidance-default-outline-discoura: The subject's own website, social media accounts, press releases, and sponsored content
Blogs, forums, and other self-published material
Sources that only mention the topic in passing without substantive coverage
articleguidance-default-outline-preload:
[Start with a short introduction: who or what the subject is and why it is notable.]

[Continue with the most relevant aspects of the topic, each supported by a source.]

communityconfiguration-articleguidance-d: Settings for the guided new-article experience on this wiki.
communityconfiguration-articleguidance-f: This setting decides whether the guided new-article experience is available on this wiki at all.
communityconfiguration-articleguidance-a: Enable article guidance on this wiki

When this is off, article guidance is not available: red links open the standard editor, the guided page cannot be used, and the personal preference is hidden. The settings below have an effect only while this is on.
communityconfiguration-articleguidance-r: These settings decide who is taken to the guided new-article experience instead of the standard editor.
communityconfiguration-articleguidance-a: Open the guided experience from red links

When enabled, following a red link to a missing article opens the guided experience instead of the standard editor. Editors who prefer the standard editor can switch this off for themselves in their preferences.

This setting has an effect only while the setting above is on. When enabled, only editors below this wiki's newer-editor edit count get the guided experience, and everyone else keeps the standard editor.
